title: How a language attaches a key to a route
description: The JSON map is the interchange format. In source, the same key may be an annotation/attribute/decorator on a method, the handler's param type(s), its return type, a named function type, or any combination. None of these are required at the JSON layer; they document provenance so generators can round-trip.

annotation.description: Attribute, decorator, or annotation on the handler method (Java @GET, Rust #[get], Dart @Rpc, Python @app.post, C# [HttpGet]).

param_types.description: Handler parameter types that imply the route (Axum extractors, Connect request message, JSON-RPC params by-name).

return_type.description: Handler return type that implies the route (Axum IntoResponse, Connect response message, OpenRPC result schema name).

function_type.description: Named function type / type alias for the handler (TypeScript UnaryFn<Req,Res>, Gleam fn(Req) -> Res, Rust type alias).

file.description: Optional extra: source file. Not required. One file may hold many HTTP verbs.

symbol.description: Optional extra: method, fn, or const name in that file.
